newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex creates 10 petrochemical units.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex creates 10 petrochemical units.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) board of directors approved the creation of 10 subsidiary companies in a meeting Friday, the state-owned oil and gas monopoly said in a statement.

The board members agreed to create 10 companies composed of secondary petrochemical plants: Cosoleacaque, La Cangrejera, Morelos, Pajaritos, Independencia, Salamanca, Ciudad Camargo, Escolin, Reynosa and Tula.
As planned in the government's privatization strategy, the new companies will be 51-percent owned by Pemex, with minority private ownership. Private companies can own a majority stake in new plants.

The new strategy "will spur Mexico's petrochemical industry through the opening of new investment routes that will make possible greater production capacity, and build a more competitive and efficient industry," Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles said in a statement.
Reyes has said private companies will be allowed to purchase part of the petrochemical plants in the first months of 1997.
